title: Probabilistic per-model & per-tenant load shedder with safe rollback and fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: During multi-tenant traffic spikes and periodic downstream model regressions we observe cascading resource exhaustion (GPU queues, KV cache pressure) that causes higher tail latency and error rates, which then amplifies through retries. Existing all-or-nothing circuit breakers are either too coarse (tenant-wide trips) or too aggressive (drop all traffic). Requirements: implement a probabilistic, fine-grained load shedder that can operate per dependency (model variant), per-model, and per-tenant; align shedding with SLOs; provide safe fallbacks (cached response, lower-cost model, user-visible degradation); and support immediate rollback and diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Feature implemented behind a feature flag and configurable per region
Per-tenant and per-model shedding policies can be configured remotely (console/API)
Shedder uses short-term error-rate and latency signals with exponential decay windows and exposes current shed rate as telemetry
Safe fallbacks implemented: 1) prefix-KV cached response 2) lower-cost quantized model 3) degraded structured response with explanation header
Canary rollout plan exists with automated health checks tied to SLOs and automatic rollback if health deteriorates
Dashboards and alerting for shed rate, p95/p99 latency, error rate, and fallback usage created
E2E tests that simulate downstream model slowdowns and tenant spikes and assert system remains within SLOs
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after postmortem of 2026-03-08 incident. TL;DR: tenant X produced burst of requests to heavyweight decoder that caused queue growth and evictions in KV cache. All-or-nothing breakers converted to full tenant trips, causing customer-visible failures. Need a graduated approach.

2026-03-11 - Miguel Santos: Drafted design doc (attached). Key idea: compute a rolling error+latency score per (region, tenant, model_variant). Use a probabilistic sampling function to decide whether to allow the request. Sampling rate = f(SLO_gap, recent_errors, queue_depth). This gives a smooth degradation curve rather than binary trip. Also include forced immediate trip condition for extreme cases (e.g., GPU OOM or backend down).

2026-03-11 - Priya Malhotra (PM): Love the gradual curve idea. Please include explicit knobs for 'graceful fallback preference' with the following priority: 1) prefix-kv cached response 2) fast quantized model (q4) 3) canned minimal response with user-facing header and telemetry. Also add per-tenant tolerance that product can configure (some enterprise tenants want aggressive isolation).

2026-03-12 - Eng infra review (comment by Lucas Chen): Observability requirements: need gauge for current_shed_rate, histogram for decisions by reason (error_rate, latency, queue_depth), and counters for fallback_type used. Suggest emitting a sample for every decision to trace back user request to decision via request_id.

2026-03-12 - Design review (comment by Elena Park): UX for console: expose a real-time slider with predicted impact and a per-tenant override panel. Also add a rollout knob and a 'dry-run' mode where decisions are logged but not applied.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Santos: Implemented prototype in runtime branch. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842. Prototype details: probabilistic function uses logistic mapping on a composed signal: 0.6*error_rate_short + 0.3*(latency_p95_norm) + 0.1*(queue_fill). Windows: short=30s expo-decay alpha=0.2, medium=5m. Default threshold mapping: SLO_gap<=0 => shed_rate 0; SLO_gap positive maps to shed_rate up to 0.6. Extreme conditions override to 1.0.

2026-03-13 - QA (comment by Janelle Wu): Added E2E tests that simulate 10x request spike to heavyweight-model in one region and introduced 50% downstream latency. With default config, we observed shed_rate ramp to ~40% and system stayed under p95 SLO for other tenants. Need additional tests for cold-cache behavior (cached fallback should not be used immediately if cache miss rate high).

2026-03-13 - PM (comment by Priya Malhotra): Approve canary rollout after small UX tweak (show expected degraded QPS estimate). Schedule canary for 2026-03-16 to 5% traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 48 hours.
